title: Love versus romance
paragraphs: Are you a hopeless romantic? Do you get excited by the idea of falling in love with the man or woman of your dreams? Does watching a romcom or a period drama on TV make you cry? Or are you someone who thinks romance is based on an idealised view of reality that doesn't really exist? Well, you could be right!

I'm no romantic and more of a realist - taking a more practical approach to love - maybe that's why I never had many girlfriends! But if you really are expecting the kind of love that makes your heart flutter with happiness you may be disappointed.

Our expectation of what romance is, probably originated from the Romantic period - an artistic, literary, musical and intellectual movement that originated in Europe in the 18th Century. The notion of falling in love, getting married and living happily ever after were culturally held ideas formed during this period and still exist today.

Of course there's nothing wrong with liking the idea of romance; it makes us feel good — but we must be careful not to use it as a benchmark for our own relationships. This idealised version of love leaves out the nitty-gritty of real-life relationships. There's usually work, finances and other stresses of everyday life to deal with. You can't expect romantic gestures like a bunch of red roses every day — there are bills to pay!

Many popular love stories end at the point where the characters get together or tie the knot. That puts the focus on finding someone special. But very few show us how to keep that perfect catch over a long period of time. A relationship is hard work. It's frustrating, messy and can be emotionally damaging.

If you're still convinced romance isn't dead, how will you ever find it? Historian and TV presenter Lucy Worsley thinks nowadays, any idea of romance is dying because it has become "too easy" to meet new people via dating apps. She told the BBC the "slow exquisite torture of love in Jane Austen novels no longer existed in the age of Grindr and Tinder [apps]."

Perhaps romance is best left to the movies - a fantasy that makes us feel good - and instead concentrate on finding a good and healthy relationship, with all its ups and downs, but with lots of love. Do you believe romance is really dead?

vocabulary.entry: hopeless romantic [n.] /ˌhəʊpləs rəʊˈmæntɪk/ 无可救药的浪漫主义者
vocabulary.example: He is a hopeless romantic who believes in love at first sight.
vocabulary.translation: 他是一个无可救药的浪漫主义者，相信一见钟情。

vocabulary.example: She loves watching romcoms on rainy afternoons.
vocabulary.translation: 她喜欢在下雨的下午看浪漫喜剧。

vocabulary.entry: idealised [adj.] /aɪˈdiːəlaɪzd/ 理想化的 (英式拼写，美式: idealized)
vocabulary.example: The film presents an idealised version of the past.
vocabulary.translation: 这部电影呈现了过去的一个理想化版本。

vocabulary.example: As a realist, she knows that life isn't always fair.
vocabulary.translation: 作为一个现实主义者，她知道生活并不总是公平的。

vocabulary.example: Her heart fluttered when she saw him.
vocabulary.translation: 她见到他时心怦怌直跳。

vocabulary.entry: originated [v.] /əˈrɪdʒɪneɪtɪd/ 起源；发源 (原形: originate)
vocabulary.example: The tradition originated in ancient China.
vocabulary.translation: 这个传统起源于古代中国。

vocabulary.example: The book is aimed at an intellectual audience.
vocabulary.translation: 这本书面向有思想修养的读者。

vocabulary.example: He has a romantic notion of life in the countryside.
vocabulary.translation: 他对乡村生活有一种浪漫的想法。

vocabulary.example: The company's performance is the benchmark for the industry.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司的业绩是该行业的基准。

vocabulary.entry: nitty-gritty [n.] /ˌnɪti ˈɡrɪti/ 具体细节；基本事实 (口语)
vocabulary.example: Let's get down to the nitty-gritty of the problem.
vocabulary.translation: 让我们深入了解问题的具体细节。

vocabulary.entry: tie the knot [phr.] /taɪ ðə nɒt/ 结婚 (口语)
vocabulary.example: They tied the knot in a small ceremony.
vocabulary.translation: 他们在一个小型仪式上结婚了。

vocabulary.example: Many people consider him a perfect catch.
vocabulary.translation: 许多人认为他是个理想伴侣。

vocabulary.example: It's frustrating when technology doesn't work.
vocabulary.translation: 当技术出问题时，真是令人沮丧。

vocabulary.example: Divorce can be a messy process.
vocabulary.translation: 离婚可能是一个棘手的过程。

vocabulary.example: She was emotionally exhausted after the argument.
vocabulary.translation: 争吵之后，她在情感上筋疲力尽。

vocabulary.example: I am convinced that he is telling the truth.
vocabulary.translation: 我确信他在说实话。

vocabulary.example: The pain was exquisite and unbearable.
vocabulary.translation: 这种疼痛剧烈而无法忍受。

vocabulary.example: Waiting for the results was pure torture.
vocabulary.translation: 等待结果纯粹是一种折磨。

vocabulary.example: He lives in a fantasy world of his own making.
vocabulary.translation: 他活在自己创造的幻想世界里。

vocabulary.entry: ups and downs [phr.] /ˌʌps ənd ˈdaʊnz/ 起伏；兴衰
vocabulary.example: Every relationship has its ups and downs.
vocabulary.translation: 每段关系都有起伏。

vocabulary.example: She enjoys watching period dramas set in the 19th century.
